Protosilylation
Stable and Recyclable Copper Nanoclusters with Exposed Active
Sites for Broad-Scope Protosilylation in Open Air
Songwei Wen<sup>+</sup>, Chengkai Zhang<sup>+</sup>, Li-Juan Liu, Zhi Wang, Di Sun,* and Jian He*
Abstract: Despite recent advances in cluster-based
catalysis for organic synthesis, the substrate scope of
reactions catalyzed by metal nanoclusters is typically not
superior to previously established catalytic systems.
Herein, we develop new atomically precise copper
nanoclusters for protosilylation, with scope expanding to
alkenes and simple enynes that were not suitable for
prior synthetic methodologies with traditional copper
complexes. The involvement of a second copper center
in the metal kernel during the migratory insertion step is
thought to be responsible for the expanded scope. In
addition, the reaction is highly compatible with water
and can be carried out in open air rather than under
inert gas protection. Mechanistic studies suggest that the
cluster-catalyzed protosilylation proceeds in the absence
of silyl radicals. The current findings demonstrate the
potential of using metal nanoclusters for practical and
sustainable chemical synthesis.
Introduction
Because of the excellent tunability of ligand scaffolds and
kernel structures, as well as the distinct photochemical
characteristics of metal cores, atomically precise metal
nanoclusters have shown promise as effective catalysts for
the development of organic chemical processes.<sup>[1]</sup> In recent
years, considerable efforts have been made toward con-
structing catalytically active copper nanoclusters in gram
scales at low cost for sustainable synthetic applications<sup>[2]</sup>
While several types of cluster-catalyzed coupling reactions
can be achieved with increased efficiency,<sup>[3]</sup> developing
robust copper nanocluster catalysts that can significantly
broaden reaction scope when compared to established
catalytic systems based on conventional copper complexes
remains a major challenge.
On account of its flat structure and strong chelating
effects, we anticipated that the incorporation of maleonitri-
ledithiolate (mnt) in cluster synthesis would produce stable
copper nanoclusters with exposed active sites suitable for
practical catalytic applications.<sup>[4]</sup> The presence of Cu�Cu
bonds in nanoclusters could have an important impact on
the elementary steps during catalysis, potentially overcom-
ing synthetic limitations in catalytic organic transformations.
Since protosilylation reactions are crucial for organic
synthesis<sup>[5]</sup> and can be facilitated by copper complexes,<sup>[6]</sup>
investigating them with novel copper nanoclusters gave us
an ideal opportunity to test the hypothesis. Even though
copper-catalyzed protosilylation of alkynes and enynes with
(dimethylphenylsilyl)boronic acid pinacol ester (pinB–
SiMe Ph), a readily available and moisture-stable silylboro-
nate, has been extensively studied through the use of various
ligands (Schemes 1a and 1b),<sup>[7]</sup> there is still room for
improvement in terms of catalyst turnover numbers (TONs)
and reaction operability.
Here we report the synthesis and characterization of
copper nanoclusters protected by mnt, thiolate, and bi-
sphosphine ligands, which efficiently catalyze protosilylation
of C�C multiple bonds under air atmosphere (Scheme 1c).
The optimized nanocatalyst can be recycled multiple runs
without loss of reactivity, and its remarkable stability is
further demonstrated by UV–Vis, NMR, and ESI-MS
studies. Aside from the high activity in gram-scale synthesis,
the newly-developed copper nanocluster exhibits outstand-
ing catalytic performance in the protosilylation of alkenes
and enynes without the need for the pre-installation of
electron-withdrawing functionalities.<sup>[7e,8]</sup> Additional interac-
tions between the silyl group and the copper center adjacent
to the exposed active site are likely to promote the key
migratory insertion step, resulting in an expanded substrate
scope in protosilylation reactions.

\mathrm { C u } _ { 6 }
nanoclusters with exposed active sites for efficiently

methodologies.
